title: Bass drummer's place in the parade band; Alessandra
summary: They discuss where the bass drummer marches and the instrumentation of the Fisher band, including peck horn player Alessandra.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Well I was going to ask about the position of the bass drummer. Was he always on the left? Always on the left, as a rule. As you marched on the left, as a rule. Yeah. The bass drummer is over on your left and you were the snare drum on the right.

Unless you like, like we here, you had two and then you put the other one in the middle. And then, in those days the trombones, and if you had two trombones, well you'd have the two trombones and the bass horn. Incidentally, in this vicious band, there's a musician who became later a legitimate musician in the Sanger Theater. He became an old boss, by the name of Alessandra. He was also a peck horn player in that band and his father was a bass player. He had one of these Italian helican basses, not the Sousa for him, but the old helican bass. He was in the band also.
